column1: # Served-artifact markers for the vendored Element Web patches (spec layer L2).
# One row per marker: entry<TAB>served-path<TAB>fixed-string. `entry` is the number of the
# registry entry in README.md. A marker is a fixed string (grep -F, no regex) that is PRESENT in
# a build that carries the entry and ABSENT from stock upstream Element Web at the same tag.
# The discrimination record (image, path, count per marker) is in README.md, section
# "Marker discrimination record".
# Served paths, relative to the webroot:
#   index.html, sw.js, sw-boot.js    the file itself
#   bundles/*/<file>                 the `*` is the bundle hash, read from index.html
#                                    (bundles/<hash>/bundle.js); use the NAMED files init.js
#                                    and element-web-app.js, not the numbered chunks (<n>.js)
#   i18n/<name>.json                 the language file whose hashed name languages.json gives
#                                    (i18n/en_EN.json is served as i18n/en_EN.<hash>.json)
# Used by dockerfiles/Dockerfile.element (fails the build when a row is missing from the
# builder's webapp), by scripts/element-patch-markers.sh (a served deployment) and by
# scripts/check-patch-registry.sh (every numbered entry has a row, no row names a missing entry).
# Rules: no tab inside a field; a marker survives minification (string literals, i18n keys,
# log messages, property and module-path strings; NOT class or function names, which are
# mangled); entry 6 uses the IndexedDB name and the labs flag, never code the cold-scan,
# eviction or redaction logic changes. Entry 8 lists only strings that the form without proof
# verification (before 2026-09-29) also has, because the baseline build predates the verifying
# form; `did_search_verified` marks that form and becomes a row once every build to be
# checked carries it.
